question: Does grammatical restriction or ambiguous segmentation rescue a fixed ordinary-concatenation table with at most22 distinct nonempty codewords covering every previously admitted whole group?
answer: No. Under the unchanged22-unit/whole-group/exact-coverage assumptions, the only such table is the set of22 singleton working units. This concerns physical codeword shapes, not recovered source-letter names or meanings.
conditional_premises: The unchanged1235validator and recordedPASS verify that all22 working units occur in W, separately for IT2a,RF1b,ZL3b; this note inherits that result and binds its bytes, without a new native replay.
The closed UD22 post-result proof excludes every freely uniquely decipherable table of at most22 entries with a longer code actually used on W. Its original1235 registered bounds remain23/22/22.

Writing is ordinary concatenation of a finite fixed set of nonempty strings. Complete recorded word groups must be covered exactly. No sourceword erasure, stroke overlap, changed units, repaired exceptions or cross-space codes are admitted.
The number22 bounds distinct codewords, not the number of visible glyph types. A22-glyph script can have more entries than22.
general_lemma: For any finite non-UD set C of distinct nonempty finite words, there exists a UD set D with fewer members than C such that every member of C is a concatenation of members of D. Consequently C* is contained in D*.
proof_outline: A nonUD finite C has a proper prefix pair v=u r. Replace v by the nonempty r. C is generated by the new set, total entry length strictly decreases and cardinality never increases.

If r is new, the original table over new abstract atoms consists of all singleton atoms except R plus UR. This is suffix-free. Therefore if the new set wereUD, so would the original be. A same-cardinality step cannot cure nonUD.
Repeating only while nonUD terminates in UD D. At least one strict cardinality reduction must occur, and C* is contained in D*. Thus |D|<|C|.

A nonUD C with |C|<=22 covering W would give UD D with at most21 entries covering W. Since W contains all22 units, some longer D-entry must be used. That contradicts the existing UD22 exclusion. If C isUD, that exclusion leaves only22 singleton entries.
grammar_consequence: Permitted source sequences form a subset of C*. Restricting this subset cannot supply a covering table C when none exists. Grammar-assisted reading therefore cannot rescue the SAME capped physical table; context-dependent production or extra entries change the premise.
correction_to_previous_scope_language: The earlier UD-only report correctly stated its own tested scope. Its suggestion that grammar-assisted writing lies outside that result must now be read with this additional consequence: grammar alone does not save an unchanged <=22-entry cover. Its original bytes and decision remain preserved; genuinely different production contracts remain outside both results.

limits: Rare-form, unit-identity and whole-group assumptions are inherited.1236shows material rare dependence of a separate prefix proof;1237shows small but recurrent discrepancies for one-compound models. Neither diagnostic supplies a global error budget or validates these as corrected readings.
The auxiliary D is a mathematical code, not an inferred medieval alphabet, physical teaching method or source vocabulary.
Identity covering remains possible and alone supplies no source-letter values, language, semantics, word-frequency fit or historical writing account.

Larger code tables, explicit abbreviation/escape systems, overlapping strokes, context-dependent spellings and changed group segmentation are not ruled out. They require complete stated rules and retain their own prior failures; they are not automatically selected.
decision: Close the ambiguous/grammar-filtered variant of the same exact<=22-entry fixed-table family. Do not start a new solver or increase a table cap merely to evade this bound. Review complete human writing rules under their real entry/spacing/semantic costs and actual predecessors.
